claims.claim: The word 'tomorrow' comes from the Greek words 'temnos' and 'horos'.
claims.note: The word 'tomorrow' is of Germanic/Old English origin, not Greek.

claims.claim: 'temnos' means 'empty' and 'horos' means 'limit'.
claims.note: These are not the etymological roots of tomorrow.

claims.claim: 'tomorrow' means 'after this day' in Latin.
claims.note: Tomorrow is not a Latin word and does not come from Latin.

claims.claim: Your heart is one of the most powerful organs in your body
It pumps blood all over your body
It delivers oxygen and nutrients to your muscles, brain, and organs so they can work efficiently
Without it, you wouldn't be able to think clearly, run, or breathe properly
Your favorite toy car moves because of magnets.
claims.note: Most toy cars move because of wheels, friction, pushes, or batteries/motors, not typically magnets.

claims.claim: Plants make their own food using sunlight and water.
claims.note: This is a correct description of photosynthesis (along with carbon dioxide).

claims.claim: Stars shine.
claims.note: Stars generate their own light through nuclear fusion.

claims.claim: Your body grows.
claims.note: Human bodies grow over time through cell division and development.

claims.claim: Months get their lengths from the Earth's orbit around the Sun, which isn't a perfect circle but an ellipse.
claims.note: Month lengths are based on historical and political decisions tied to the solar year and lunar cycle, not on the elliptical nature of Earth's orbit.

claims.claim: The ancient Romans divided the year into twelve months, giving us the current system.
February has fewer days because it was originally added to keep the calendar in sync with the seasons over thousands of years.
claims.note: February was the leftover period in the Roman calendar, not added later to sync the calendar over thousands of years.

claims.claim: Electric cars run on electricity instead of gasoline.
Electric cars have big batteries that store energy.
When you press the gas pedal, they turn that electricity into wheels spinning.
They are much better for the environment because they don't make any pollution.
Planes fly in the sky because they have powerful engines that push them forward
air is always moving around them
The wings of the plane are shaped like curves so the air flows smoothly over them
creating lift just like a bird's wings
The biggest planet in our solar system is Jupiter.
Jupiter is a giant ball of gas and ice.
Jupiter is way bigger than all the other planets put together.
Rhythm is the music's heartbeat, like when you tap your foot or clap along to the song.
claims.note: Tapping your foot or clapping along to a song is generally considered the beat, not the rhythm.

claims.claim: Beat is what makes that tapping or clapping sound strong and steady.
Beat is like when you hear someone counting 'one, two, three, four!'.
Trains are designed to be long because they need a lot of space to carry heavy loads.
Trains need to be long to safely travel at high speeds over long distances without losing power or control.
claims.note: Train length does not inherently help maintain high speeds, power, or control; in fact, very long freight trains often travel slower and require distributed power systems to maintain control.

claims.claim: Longer trains mean that the train cars can share the weight, making them more efficient.
Longer trains reduce the amount of energy needed to move them.
claims.note: Longer trains do not reduce the total amount of energy needed to move them; rather, they increase the total energy required, though they are more fuel-efficient per ton of cargo compared to running many separate smaller trains.

claims.claim: A pumpkin is orange.
A pumpkin gets its orange color from the yummy seeds inside.
claims.note: The orange color comes from pigments like carotenoids in the skin and flesh of the pumpkin, not from the seeds.

claims.claim: Singing in the shower is a fun tradition that has been around for a long time.
Singing helps wash away bad feelings or tension you might be carrying.
Singing helps keep your immune system healthy by releasing endorphins.
Endorphins are chemicals in your brain that make you feel good.
Berries are full of healthy things like fiber and vitamins.
Berries help keep your tummy happy.
Berries give you energy to play.
We celebrate New Year's Day on January 1st because it was originally set as the beginning of the Roman calendar
The Roman calendar was based on the cycles of the moon rather than the sun
claims.note: The Julian calendar introduced by Julius Caesar was a solar calendar, not a lunar one.

claims.claim: The Romans chose January 1st because it was the first day of the month
claims.note: January 1st was chosen because it was when Roman consuls began their terms in office, later dedicated to Janus.

claims.claim: The Gregorian calendar shifted the date forward by eleven days due to a mistake in calculating leap years
claims.note: The Gregorian calendar correction (ten days, not eleven) was made to correct the accumulated drift of the Julian calendar's solar year calculation, not a single eleven-day shift.

claims.claim: 1900 wasn't a leap year, but 2000 was
Ice floats because it is less dense than water.
Water molecules form hydrogen bonds in a hexagonal structure, which creates a rigid lattice.
When water freezes into ice, the molecules slow down and pack closer together into a crystalline structure, making the overall density lower.
claims.note: Molecules actually pack further apart, not closer together, when water freezes, which is why it expands and becomes less dense.

claims.claim: This unique property of ice is why you can stack ice cubes on top of each other without them sinking.
Using public transportation, biking, or walking instead of driving alone reduces your carbon footprint.
Turning off lights and electronics when you're not using them reduces your carbon footprint.
Choosing energy-efficient appliances reduces your carbon footprint.
Eating less meat has a bigger carbon footprint than plant-based foods.
Buying second-hand clothes instead of new ones reduces your carbon footprint.
A banana tastes sweet.
A banana is yellow.
When you blow air into the balloon, it gets bigger and bigger.
Blowing air into a balloon makes it go up high in the sky.
claims.note: Blowing normal breath into a balloon makes it heavier than air, so it does not float up on its own.

claims.claim: Friends care about us and listen when we have a story to tell.
Friends share fun things with us.
When you laugh or play together, your brain releases special chemicals called endorphins.
Endorphins make you feel great inside.
Having a budget helps you manage your money to achieve goals like saving for a car or traveling.
A budget helps with paying off debt and managing everyday expenses.
A budget gives you a clear picture of how much you earn and spend each month.
Budgeting helps you avoid overspending and build financial stability.
It is completely normal to feel a little bit scared of the dark.
Your body's built-in alarm system, called the amygdala, picks up on this change and triggers feelings of fear or anxiety.
As you grow older, your brain develops more mature ways of processing fear.
Galaxies are giant collections of billions of stars, gas, dust, and dark matter held together by gravity.
Stars are the main luminous objects within galaxies.
Galaxies contain vast amounts of interstellar gas and dust that glow in infrared light.
The most massive and brightest galaxies can have supermassive black holes at their centers.
Understanding the composition of galaxies helps us study the history of the universe and how it formed over billions of years.
Mixing blue and yellow together results in green.
Flowers come in all sorts of colors and shapes, like roses, daisies, and sunflowers.
Some flowers make yummy food for animals.
Flowers smell nice.
Spicy foods contain compounds called capsaicinoids, which are found in chili peppers.
Capsaicinoids interact with special pain sensors in your tongue and nose called TRPV1 receptors.
TRPV1 receptors send signals to your brain that make it feel like the heat is spreading all over your mouth.
Allergies happen when your immune system mistakes harmless things like pollen, dust, or certain foods for threats.
The immune system normally fights off bad germs like bacteria and viruses.
The immune system sends out too many protective chemicals called antibodies during an allergic reaction.
Allergic reactions can cause symptoms like sneezing, itchy eyes, or even trouble breathing.
Some people inherit genes that make their immune systems more sensitive.
Other people might be exposed to allergens early in life which affects allergies.
Butterflies fly to find yummy flowers to eat
Butterflies use their long tongues to sip sweet nectar
Sipping sweet nectar helps butterflies grow big and strong
Day and night happen because the Earth is spinning like a giant ball.
As the Earth spins, one half faces the sun and gets bright daylight.
The other half of the Earth is facing away from the sun and gets dark nighttime.
The cycle of day and night is like a fun game that keeps us all safe.
Rainbows happen because of raindrops.
Raindrops catch the sunlight.
Raindrops bend the light.
Raindrops make light split into all the colors of the rainbow.
Yucky smells happen when food gets old or gets in contact with things it shouldn't.
Tiny bugs and germs can grow on the food, making it taste and smell yucky.
